name: Sheshan
overview: Sheshan is a male member of the tribe of Judah, noted specifically as the son of Ishi according to 1 Chronicles 2:31. Beyond this genealogical detail, Scripture provides limited information about his life or role. His mention serves primarily to establish lineage within the tribe of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Sheshan appears as a proper name in Scripture, with no recorded meaning or divine origin noted in the biblical text. It is simply presented as the personal name of this individual without additional title or significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Sheshan as the son of Ishi. It is also inferred that Ahlai is his father, and Jarha is considered his master based on related genealogical context in 1 Chronicles 2:31 and 2:34. These relationships situate him within the Judahite family structure and social setting.
scriptureSignificance: Sheshan's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of Judah, which is foundational for understanding the lineage of God's chosen people. His mention underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving the tribe of Judah through successive generations. While not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion affirms the continuity of God's covenant promises through the descendants of Judah.
